name: Peloton Interactive, Inc.

groups.label: All holders: 180-day lock-up / market standoff from the prospectus date (early end for a trading blackout cannot be dated)
groups.groupNote: Filing pp.142-143 and 150: directors, executive officers and substantially all holders are subject to 'lock-up agreements or market standoff provisions' for at least 180 days, with the same blackout proviso written against the lock-up period. The filing does not say which agreement an early employee signed; both seats are given the same date.

tranches.quote: not to dispose of or hedge any of our or their common stock or securities convertible into or exchangeable for shares of common stock during the period from the date of this prospectus continuing through the date 180 days after the date of this prospectus, except with the prior written consent of Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC and J.P. Morgan Securities LLC; provided that if (1) at least 120 days have elapsed since the date of this prospectus, (2) we have publicly released our earnings results for the quarterly period during which this offering occurred, and (3) such lock-up period is scheduled to end during or within five trading days prior to a blackout period, such lock-up period will end ten trading days prior to the commencement of such blackout period.
tranches.readA: 100% locked through day 180 (2020-03-23), free 2020-03-24; blackout early end not datable
tranches.readB: 100% day 181 -> 2020-03-24; blackout early end not datable
tranches.reconcilerNote: Both reads agree on 100%, trigger and date; they differ only in how much of the quote they copied (A included the consent clause, B stopped before it; the final quote includes the whole sentence with the blackout proviso). Prospectus dated 2019-09-25 (p.1 cover). 'Continuing through the date 180 days after' = 2020-03-23 (Mon); Shares Eligible (p.142) says 'beginning 181 days after the date of this prospectus' = 2020-03-24 (Tue), a trading day in base.json. The early-end proviso needs 120 days (2020-01-23), results for the quarter of the offering (Q1 FY20, released 2019-11-05) and a blackout under the insider trading policy; the policy dates are not in the filing, so no earlier date can be computed. Later date 2020-03-24 used (cannot let a player sell early).

headlines.text: Shares plunge as vaccine news pulls investors from pandemic favorites
Company cuts full-year forecast, citing softer demand and limited visibility
Shares tumble on report that company is pausing production
New chief executive named; company announces restructuring and large job cuts
Quarterly results beat company forecasts as cash burn narrows sharply
Paying users decline in quarter as demand slows and recall costs mount
Full-year revenue guided lower; company says it will miss cash-flow goal
Second straight quarter of positive cash flow; revenue returns to growth

reveal.text: Peloton priced its IPO on September 25, 2019 at $29 a share and closed its first day at $25.76, below the offer. The stock peaked at $167.42 on January 13, 2021, fell to a low of $2.88 on August 14, 2024, and closed the five years at $4.68 on September 30, 2024, 83.9% below the offer price. Its filings show pandemic demand fading, then repeated forecast cuts, restructuring and leadership changes as sales slowed.

notes: Prospectus figure is after the offering and the concurrent private placement of 3,448,275 shares.
